title.rendered: The Samaritan Woman: Living Water: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again.” A morning devotional on the woman at the well and the Water your soul is looking for.

content.rendered:
Noon at Jacob’s well. The wrong time of day to fetch water. The other women of the village had come and gone before the heat. She came alone at noon because she could not face them. And there she found a Jewish rabbi waiting.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, September 8, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Jesus answered and said to her, ‘Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.'”
John 4:13-14 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Noon at Jacob’s well, outside the Samaritan village of Sychar. The wrong time of day to fetch water. The other women of the village had come at dawn and again in the cool of the evening. She came alone at noon because she could not face them. Five failed marriages behind her, and now a sixth man she was not married to. The whispers of the village had followed her for years. It was easier to walk the extra distance in the midday heat than to hear the whispers one more time. And there, alone at the well, she found a Jewish rabbi waiting. He should not have been there. Jews did not travel through Samaria if they could help it. And Jewish rabbis did not speak to strange women, especially not Samaritan ones. But this rabbi asked her for a drink.

The conversation that followed is one of the longest recorded dialogues Jesus ever had with any individual, and it is with a Samaritan woman whose life had unravelled. She sparred with Him about ritual water. He gently turned the conversation to a deeper thirst. “Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.” He knew the ache underneath her many attempts at love. He knew that no husband, and no man in her life, had ever satisfied the deepest thirst of her soul. And He was offering her Himself as the only water that would finally, permanently, satisfy it.

The Passion Translation captures the beauty of the exchange: “But if anyone drinks the living water I give them, they will never thirst again and will be forever satisfied! For when you drink the water I give you it becomes a gushing fountain of the Holy Spirit, springing up and flooding you with endless life!” (John 4:14 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But whoever takes a drink of the water that I will give him shall never, no never, be thirsty any more. But the water that I will give him shall become a spring of water welling up (flowing, bubbling) within him unto (into, for) eternal life” (John 4:14 AMPC). Never, no never, be thirsty any more. That is the promise of the living water Jesus was offering her, and offers still today.

The Samaritan woman did what she had never done in decades. She dropped her water jar and ran back into the village she had been avoiding, calling out to the very people whose eyes she had been dodging, “Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?” Shame did not chain her to the well anymore. She had met a Man who knew everything about her and loved her anyway, and she could not keep it to herself. The whole village came out to Jesus that day. Many believed. It is one of the earliest recorded revivals in the New Testament, and it started with one woman at noon at a well who had almost given up on being seen.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the invitation still standing at every well of your life. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if you have been drinking from wells that leave you thirsty again, career wells, relationship wells, achievement wells, approval wells, entertainment wells, Jesus is still offering the water no other source can offer. Living water. Springing up. Endless life. The wells of this world always leave the soul thirsty again. The water Jesus gives satisfies for eternity. Drink today. And do not be surprised if, once you have drunk, you find yourself running back to the very village you had been avoiding, telling people what He has done.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is the source of living water. Every other well I have drunk from has left me thirsty again. Career. Relationships. Achievement. Approval. Entertainment. None of them have satisfied the deepest thirst of my soul. Today I come to Jesus. I drink. I let His Spirit spring up in me as an endless fountain. And I trust that the same Jesus who met the Samaritan woman with knowledge and love knows me completely and loves me anyway. I refuse to hide at noon anymore. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is my living water. I drink from Him today. The endless fountain of the Holy Spirit springs up in me. I am fully known and fully loved.
